summary: The study demonstrates the use of atomic layer deposition (ALD) to create quantum-confined ZnO nanostructures on both two-dimensional (Si wafers) and three-dimensional (SiO2 particles) substrates. The process involves the use of diethylzinc and hydrogen peroxide as precursors at 100°C, resulting in conformal, pinhole-free films. The films exhibit quantum confinement effects, leading to a blue-shift in the bandgap as the crystallite size decreases. The study also explores the impact of thermal annealing on crystallite size and bandgap modulation.
evidence: Polycrystalline ZnO films ranging from ∼1.5 to 15 nm in thickness were deposited via ALD using diethylzinc and hydrogen peroxide at 100°C. The ZnO bandgap was increasingly blue-shifted for films of decreasing crystallite size, approaching +0.3 eV at dimensions of 2–3 nm. Post-deposition annealing steps increased the crystallite size of the films, independently of the coating thickness.
